events.description: A sudden bright flash and fireball appear at ~7.5 s (f3), rapidly expanding into a large fire and dense black smoke plume by f4–f6, consistent with a single explosive event followed by burning debris.

verification.reason: Frames f3–f6 show the classic progression of an explosion: initial detonation (f3), fireball and fragmentation (f4), and rapid smoke column development (f5–f6); later frames (f7–f10) show only smoke dispersion, not new explosions. Candidates 0, 1, and 2 all describe overlapping intervals of this same event; merged accordingly.

events.description: A second distinct explosion occurs around 16.0–17.0 s (f14–f15), producing a new fireball and rising smoke column separate from the first, visible through f23.

verification.reason: At f14, a new bright flash and fireball appear in a different location (lower right) while the first smoke plume is still visible left/center; f15–f23 show sustained smoke from this second source, indicating a separate explosive event. Candidates 3–6 all refer to parts of this second event; merged into one interval covering its full visible duration.
